# zstd, the decoder only

Upstream: https://github.com/facebook/zstd, tag v1.5.6 (`794ea1b0afca0f020f4e57b6732332231fb23c70 2024-03-21`), BSD licence
(LICENSE; zstd is dual BSD/GPLv2, and the BSD terms are the ones used here).

`zstddeclib.c` is upstream's own single-file decoder, generated by
`build/single_file_libs/create_single_file_decoder.sh` and not edited;
`zstd.h` is `lib/zstd.h`.

Why: a RustDesk client compresses file-transfer blocks and clipboard text
with zstd whenever that is smaller, so receiving either needs a real decoder
(sending does not: a frame of raw blocks is valid zstd, which is what
`src/core/session.c` writes).

It is built with `HUF_FORCE_DECOMPRESS_X1`,
`ZSTD_FORCE_DECOMPRESS_SEQUENCES_SHORT` and `ZSTD_NO_INLINE` at `-O2`: 52 KB
of 68k code instead of 86 KB, for a decoder that only ever sees 128 KB
blocks. It allocates its context (~100 KB) with malloc, so it runs in the
Mac's main loop, never at interrupt time.
